title: Remove student uploads from public media library
body:
Currently all files uploaded by learners as quiz answers, are stored in the media library, so they are publicly accessible by the direct link.

We should come up with a way to hide these files from the media library and prevent them from being publicly accessed.

501931-zd-woothemes
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body: In WP Job Manager, I believe we simply tack on a random string/hash to the file slug so that it's much harder to guess the URL. But even if we somehow hid files from the Media Library, you'd still be uploading files to a webserver, so IMHO it's never going to be 100% safe.

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body: @pgk any update on this and when the 1.9.12 release might be done? I have a user asking!

comments.author: Participant 4
comments.body: the 1.9.12 release is allready in production @annezazuu so this problem must be fixed in another release. I asked again, because I see no progress or movement here too. Other course plugins I have (wp-courseware, Learndash), don't save students uploads in the media library. Images in the media library are also cropped in various sizes and for student uploads that is unnecessary, so the normal media library function is not that handy for student uploads.

comments.author: Participant 4
comments.body: There doesn't seem to be any movement on this issue. Is there any sight on when it will be taken on?

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body: @hansschuijff we don't have an ETA at this time.

comments.author: Participant 4
comments.body: How does this issue relate to the current European privacy legislation? I don't think it covers making private content public is allowed in that, at least not with explicit consent. Why isn't this solved yet? I also notice that students tend to upload the same image multiple times, which might, which can mean the dialog isn't clear for them too.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body:
We are not legal experts, so if you need advice on the legislation, we suggest you consult an attorney.

That said, having these files publicly accessible is not our intention, so I've changed this to a 'bug' rather than an 'enhancement'.

Our proposed solution is to obfuscate the file url with a random string, so that they won't be publicly available/guessable/browseable. I can't provide a timeline at this stage, but we do intend to get this fixed.

scope: Current retrievable issue body and issue comments; not the original study's historical snapshot. Linked pages and attachments are not fetched.
